t: A Greek kingdom on both shores of the Kerch Strait, ruled from Panticapaeum (modern Kerch) by the Spartocid dynasty for over three centuries.
Its grain exports helped feed classical Athens, which honoured its kings with citizenship, privileges and crowns.
It passed to Mithridates VI of Pontus and then lived on as a Roman client kingdom until the Hunnic invasions.
dyk: Jewish communities in Panticapaeum freed slaves in the synagogue and recorded it on stone; one such manumission inscription dates from 81 CE.
ev: The Archaeanactids unite the Greek cities around Panticapaeum
Spartocus I takes power, founding the Spartocid dynasty
Leucon I takes Theodosia and grants Athens privileges in the grain trade
Civil war between the sons of Paerisades I; Eumelus wins the throne
Paerisades V hands the kingdom to Mithridates VI of Pontus
Mithridates VI dies at Panticapaeum; Pharnaces II becomes a Roman client king
Rome replaces Mithridates, son of Aspurgus, with Cotys I
The Huns overrun the region and the kingdom disappears

f.founder: Spartocus I (Spartocid dynasty); earlier the Archaeanactids
f.successor: Hunnic Empire; later Byzantine Empire (city of Bosporus)
